description: Realistic analyst questions over the financial-report corpus, graded on ANSWERABILITY rather than rank. The retrieval benchmark (queries.json) asks 'is the gold page in the top 10'; this asks the question that matters to a caller: could the question be answered correctly and completely from the returned payload alone? Wrong attribution (a figure belonging to a different segment, company or year, presented where the answer should be) counts as a failure, not a hit -- it is worse than returning nothing. Reference facts are hand-verified against extracted page text; the judge compares the payload against them and never supplies ground truth itself. Single-document questions (ids prefixed sd-) are scoped to the one filing that answers them, so document selection is off the table and what remains is within-document retrieval and excerpt quality. Each question carries an explicit `scope`: "single-doc" questions are answerable from one filing and are used by the single-document eval; "multi-doc" questions need several filings and are what exercise decomposition, doc_match_counts and discoverability in the corpus eval. Filter on `scope` -- ids are opaque identifiers and their prefixes carry no meaning (the sd- prefix on some ids records only when they were added, not their scope).
